ENFORCEMENT RULE OF THE ACT ON THE EMPLOYMENT IMPROVEMENT OF DOMESTIC WORKERS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Rule is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on the Employment Improvement of Domestic Workers and the Enforcement Decree of that Act, and matters necessary for their enforcement.

Article 2 (Applications for Certification, etc.)
(1) A person who intends to obtain certification as a domestic service provider under Article 7 (2) of the Act on the Employment Improvement of Domestic Workers (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") shall submit an application for certification as a domestic service provider in Form No. 1, accompanied by the following documents, to the head of the regional employment and labor office having jurisdiction over the location of the principal place of business (hereinafter referred to as the "competent regional employment and labor office"):
  1. One copy of the business plan in Form No. 2;
  2. One copy of the articles of incorporation;
  3. One copy of the worker roster in Form No. 3 or the domestic worker employment plan in Form No. 4;
  4. One copy of a document verifying the exclusive-use floor area of the office: Provided, That this shall not apply where the person engages in fee-charging job placement services under the Employment Security Act and meets the office requirements under the relevant statutes and regulations;
  5. One copy of a document, such as a copy of a liability insurance policy, verifying that means of compensation for personal injury and property damage under Article 7 (1) 3 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "means of compensation for damage") have been secured;
  6. One copy of a document verifying that means of requesting the handling of grievances, etc. under Article 7 (1) 4 of the Act have been secured;
  7. If a representative or executive officer is a foreign national, one copy of a document certifying that the person does not fall under any subparagraph of Article 8 of the Act and authenticated, pursuant to the Act on Notarial Acts Done at Overseas Diplomatic and Consular Missions, by the consul in charge of notarial affairs at a diplomatic or consular mission of the Republic of Korea in the country concerned, consisting of either a document issued by the government or another competent authority of that country or a statement by the applicant notarized by a notary public.
(2) The public official in charge who receives the application under paragraph (1) shall verify the following documents through joint use of administrative information under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act: Provided, That, where the applicant does not consent to verification of the certificate of business registration, the official shall require the applicant to attach that document:
  1. A certificate of registered corporate matters;
  2. A certificate of business registration.
(3) The head of the competent regional employment and labor office who receives an application for certification under paragraph (1) shall examine whether the certification standards are met and notify the applicant of the result within 20 days.
(4) Where, as a result of the examination under paragraph (3), the certification standards are met and certification as a domestic service provider is granted, the head of the competent regional employment and labor office shall issue to the applicant a certificate of domestic service provider in Form No. 5 (hereinafter referred to as the "certificate"), and publicly disclose the list of certified domestic service providers and their certification numbers through the computerized system under Article 19 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "computerized system").
(5) A domestic service provider may apply for reissuance of a certificate if it has been lost or has become unusable. In this case, the provider shall submit an application for reissuance of a certificate of domestic service provider in Form No. 6 to the head of the competent regional employment and labor office.
(6) The head of the competent regional employment and labor office who receives an application for reissuance of a certificate under paragraph (5) shall reissue the certificate to the applicant within 5 days.

Article 3 (Changes to Certified Matters)
(1) "Important matters prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Employment and Labor" in Article 7 (4) of the Act means the following:
  1. Trade name or corporate name;
  2. Representative or executive officers;
  3. Location of the principal place of business.
(2) A domestic service provider that intends to change a matter specified in any subparagraph of paragraph (1) of this Article pursuant to Article 7 (4) of the Act shall submit an application for certification of changes to a domestic service provider in Form No. 7, accompanied by a copy of the certificate and the documents according to the following classifications, to the head of the competent regional employment and labor office:
  1. A change to the trade name or corporate name: One copy of a document verifying the changed details;
  2. A change to a representative or executive officer: One copy of the document under Article 2 (1) 7 (only where the new representative or executive officer is a foreign national);
  3. A change to the location of the principal place of business: One copy of a document verifying the changed details.
(3) The head of the competent regional employment and labor office who receives an application for certification of changes under paragraph (2) shall examine whether to certify the changes and notify the applicant of the result within 14 days. In this case, where the changes are certified, the head shall collect the previously issued certificate and issue a new certificate.
(4) A domestic service provider that intends to change any of the following matters pursuant to Article 7 (4) of the Act shall submit a report of changes to a domestic service provider in Form No. 7, accompanied by a copy of the certificate and the documents according to the following classifications, to the head of the competent regional employment and labor office:
  1. A change to the types of domestic services provided: One copy of the business plan in Form No. 2;
  2. A change to the means of compensation for damage: One copy of a document verifying the changed details;
  3. A change to whether domestic services are also provided under other statutes: One copy of the business plan in Form No. 2.

Article 4 (Matters to Be Disclosed by Domestic Service Providers)
(1) "Matters prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Employment and Labor" in Article 9 (1) of the Act means the following:
  1. Areas where domestic services are available;
  2. Matters concerning procedures for reporting and handling inconveniences arising while using domestic services;
  3. Means of compensation for damage;
  4. Whether domestic services are also provided under other statutes.
(2) "Methods prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Employment and Labor, such as posting on the website" in Article 9 (1) of the Act means all of the following methods:
  1. Posting on the computerized system;
  2. Posting on the website of the domestic service provider (only where the provider has a website).

Article 5 (Reports of Business Suspension, etc.)
(1) Where a domestic service provider suspends its business, it shall submit a report of business suspension in Form No. 8, accompanied by a copy of the certificate, to the head of the competent regional employment and labor office within 7 days from the date of suspension pursuant to Article 10 of the Act.
(2) Where a domestic service provider that has reported business suspension under paragraph (1) extends the reported period of suspension, it shall submit a report of extension of the period of business suspension in Form No. 8, accompanied by a copy of the certificate, to the head of the competent regional employment and labor office within 7 days from the date on which the reported period of suspension ends.
(3) Where a domestic service provider that has submitted a report of business suspension or extension of the period of business suspension under paragraph (1) or (2) intends to resume the suspended business before the reported period of suspension ends, it shall submit a report of business resumption in Form No. 8, accompanied by a copy of the certificate, to the head of the competent regional employment and labor office no later than 7 days before the intended date of resumption.
(4) Where a domestic service provider closes its business, it shall submit a report of business closure in Form No. 9, accompanied by the original certificate, to the head of the competent regional employment and labor office within 7 days from the date of closure pursuant to Article 10 of the Act: Provided, That, where the original certificate cannot be attached due to loss or another reason, stating that reason in the report of business closure may substitute for attaching the original certificate.
(5) The head of the competent regional employment and labor office who receives a report under paragraphs (1) through (4) shall disclose that fact on the computerized system.

Article 6 (Matters to Be Included in Contracts for Use) "Matters prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Employment and Labor" in Article 11 (1) 7 of the Act means the following:
  1. Details of the domestic services;
  2. Methods and procedures for changing the details, dates and hours of provision of domestic services;
  3. Methods and procedures for cancelling an application to use domestic services and terminating the contract;
  4. Matters concerning measures during the domestic worker's holidays and leave;
  5. Matters concerning resolution of disputes between domestic workers and users of domestic services.

Article 7 (Forms Relating to Criminal History Inquiries)
(1) The request for a criminal history inquiry under the part preceding the subparagraphs of Article 3 (1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Employment Improvement of Domestic Workers (hereinafter referred to as the "Decree") shall be in Form No. 10, and the consent of the person subject to the criminal history inquiry under subparagraph 2 of that paragraph shall be in Form No. 11.
(2) The request for a criminal history inquiry under the first sentence of the part preceding the subparagraphs of Article 3 (2) of the Decree shall be in Form No. 12, and the confirmation document of the domestic service provider under subparagraph 2 of that paragraph shall be a copy of the certificate of that domestic service provider.
(3) The reply to a criminal history inquiry under Article 3 (3) of the Decree shall be in Form No. 13 where requested under paragraph (1) of that Article, and in Form No. 14 where requested under paragraph (2) of that Article.

Article 8 (Methods and Subjects of Fact-Finding Surveys)
(1) A fact-finding survey under Article 21 of the Act may be conducted by interviews, telephone surveys or other methods.
(2) A fact-finding survey under paragraph (1) may include matters that the Minister of Employment and Labor deems necessary to improve the quality of domestic services and the working conditions of domestic workers.
(3) Matters necessary for the timing, procedures and methods, etc. of fact-finding surveys, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) and (2), shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Employment and Labor.

ADDENDUM <Ordinance of the Ministry of Employment and Labor No. 354, June 9, 2022>
This Rule shall enter into force on June 16, 2022.

INSTRUCTIONS

□ This business plan forms the basis for deciding whether to grant certification and must therefore be completed truthfully and in detail.

1. Institution applying for certification

○ In field ①, enter both the trade name and the corporate name if the trade name of the place of business engaged in providing domestic services differs from the corporate name.
○ In field ②, enter the name of the representative director of the corporation.

2. Plan for separate operation where domestic services are provided under other statutes

○ Complete this section only if domestic services are also provided under other statutes. Describe specifically how "the provision of domestic services under other statutes" and "the provision of domestic services in the capacity of a domestic service provider certified under this Act" will be operated separately.

3. Types of domestic services provided

○ Indicate all types of domestic services that, as a domestic service provider, you intend to provide to users through domestic workers directly employed by you.
○ If a service you intend to provide is not listed, mark "Other services" and specify the type of service in the parentheses.

4. Domestic worker employment status

○ In field ①, enter the number of domestic workers regularly employed as of the date of application for certification.
○ In field ②, enter the number of persons planned to be regularly employed as domestic workers if certification is granted upon the application.
※ If the number of regularly employed domestic workers does not reach at least 5 within 30 days from the date of certification, you may be subject to a corrective order under Article 23 (1) 2 of the Act on the Employment Improvement of Domestic Workers; failure to comply with the corrective order may result in revocation of certification under Article 23 (2) 2 of that Act.
○ In field ③, enter the number of management personnel separately employed, in addition to domestic workers, to manage domestic workers. If the number of domestic workers is less than 50, the representative may also serve as management personnel.

5. Capital

○ Enter the capital owned by the for-profit corporation only if it is a for-profit corporation.

6. If space is insufficient, an additional sheet may be prepared and attached.
